planner_decision: The b12 r1 board run (4,470 frames, both slots correct at 2,592,000 B) proves H4: store AR=883, PAXI AR=883, PAXI R=882, stale=0, ar_pending=1, af_rvalid=0, ddr_rdy=1, rd_wait_cycles saturated, raw_rd_idx=882/129,600. The DDR accepted the 883rd AR and never returned R; the stop point moved from 1176 to 882, so it is an intermittent lost read response (refresh/read-write arbitration), not a fixed address bug. The user selected option A: DDR read timeout + retry. Freeze the semantics: after an accepted AR has no R for TIMEOUT_N=8192 clk_a1, abort the current frame read, keep the slot READING (no publish, no overwrite of READY), pulse rd_timeout to the top/arbiter/bridge; the bridge clears ar_pending, drains AF, discards RF/skid and swallows any late R with ar_pending=0 for a guard window; no new AR during GUARD_N=32768 clk_a1 and the bridge guard is 65536 clk_ddr; then retry the SAME frame from word 0, up to MAX_RETRY=2 (3 attempts), then free the slot and give up. A retry re-opens the raw slot through the normal rd_open path so the A+ core restarts cleanly and the compressed slot is aborted; no descriptor is pushed without a1_commit, so no half frame is exported. Add v5 status fields timeout/retry/giveup/stale (241 B / 59 fields). Do not touch the A+ core, crop, frame format, SDC/pins/clock, or DDR IP/PAXI. The user explicitly ruled a thin-margin candidate acceptable under the b12 rule (+0.003 with 0 violations, caveat), so the build floor is +0.003 and the target is +0.05.
